observation_source.source_policy: Fresh KMA API Hub station-date observations; source values > -90 for temperature; RN_DAY=-9 maps to zero following kmahub; other negative rain values excluded and audited. Daily equal-weight means of actual valid contributors, minimum50, no imputation or 62/n scaling.
observation_source.required_stations_policy: Preserves supplied package minimum50; NOT a KMA API QC flag.
observation_source.qc_flag_origin: Derived validity/count checks on returned measurements, not independent instrument QC.

observation_policy_scope: Selected-source outputs: daily station count >=50; use actual-n daily means, including 61/60; no 62/n scaling or raw-station imputation. Policy/calendar validation is a separate training audit.
oracle: Independent Counter/fsum equal-year masses, binary-search scalar interpolation, manual tie midranks; no production distribution, np.interp or scipy rankdata.
issued_quantile_convention: Linear interpolation on sorted individual member positions (i+0.5)/M, clipped endpoints. Repeated atoms retained. Training curves instead merge ties into mass midpoints, exactly as the declared production convention.
crossing_convention: Stable RAW order; meaningful decreases and pair inversions exceed 1e-10; exact negative adjacent counts also retained. Negative-adjacent cases are counted separately from positive-valued cases.

interpretation.classification: A passing oracle establishes numerical implementation of the declared finite-sample formula, not monotonicity, distribution-level change preservation, physical realism or superior forecast skill.
interpretation.roundoff_check: The primary oracle uses accurately summed equal-year weights, not the production cumulative-sum rounding pattern. Every case is also compared against an independently coded scalar replay of that floating operation order, still using manual interpolation/midranks. Primary absolute 1e-10 exceedances are retained, checked with 50-digit Decimal, and never silently reclassified as strict numerical passes. This distinguishes tiny accumulation sensitivity from an algebra or data-pairing defect.
interpretation.annual_weighting: Each accepted source year has mass 1/N and each member in year y has mass 1/(N*M_y). Duplicating one complete year's ensemble cannot change QM/QDM. Actual equal M_y within a case makes pooled member weighting coincidentally equivalent; unequal synthetic years test the distinction.
interpretation.cdf_convention: Merged-tie probability midpoints with linear interpolation are a plotting-position distribution approximation, not the right-continuous step ECDF. Endpoint clipping and midpoint conventions are deliberate method choices.
interpretation.crossing_math: At original forecast midrank p, additive QDM is x+Qo(p)-Qh(p); the difference between adjacent corrected ranks can be negative when the historical quantile increment exceeds the forecast plus observed increments. Rainfall ratios likewise need not be monotone. This alone is not a coding bug. The issued sorted ensemble has a valid monotone quantile function, but generally not the original-rank prescribed values.
interpretation.change_preservation: For temperature the original-label identity y-Qo=x-Qh holds up to roundoff. For rain y/Qo=x/Qh holds only when Qh>=0.1 and Qo>0. After sorting, the JSON reports the actual issued Q(p) minus the original-p formula and non-dry positive-Qo ratio residuals. No universal distribution-level rank-change preservation is asserted.
interpretation.dry_rule: Qh<0.1 mm substitutes Qo instead of an unbounded ratio; this can turn raw zero into positive rain and explicitly sacrifices multiplicative change preservation. Qh=0.1 is the wet branch. With Qh>=0.1 the multiplier Qo/Qh is bounded by max(training observations)/0.1 for each case, but can still amplify extremes.
interpretation.qm_tails: QM is nondecreasing and lies within the historical observational range. It can flatten out-of-support extremes and create ties; equality to observation endpoints may begin before the historical model support ends. It does not preserve extrapolated changes. QDM is not constrained to that empirical range.
interpretation.tied_endpoint_qualification: np.interp(target,H_unique,H_midpositions) clamps below the minimum to half its tied probability mass, NOT to CDF 0; above maximum it clamps to 1 minus half the maximum mass, NOT CDF 1. Consequently the clipped mapped values need not equal observational extrema. Endpoints and zero masses are quantified on all actual cases, separating out-of-support members from members exactly at a tied endpoint. This is a midrank plotting-position variant, not the step empirical CDF.
interpretation.zero_occurrence_policy: A deterministic value-only map sends all members in the same zero atom to the same value; it cannot in general split that atom to match an arbitrary observational zero frequency. Observed zero frequency and forecast zero frequency also concern different climate/conditional populations. A randomized or explicitly rank-based wet-day/zero-occurrence policy would be a substantive method change, not a silent arithmetic fix. Claims of full CDF matching or occurrence-frequency matching need qualification.
interpretation.temperature_realism: Negative Celsius temperatures are not invalid. No arbitrary physical temperature cutoff is imposed. Actual min/max and counts outside each training observational range are reported as diagnostics, not proof of unrealistic temperatures; there is no supplied physical validity criterion. Rainfall nonnegativity and all-member finiteness are directly checked.
interpretation.forecast_vs_climate: analysis/calibration.py:165 estimates F_f using the weather ensemble for one issue/lead, not a future-climate time-window distribution. These estimate different conditional populations. Ensemble exchangeability, representativeness, stable model-observation quantile bias and adequate sample sizes would be needed to motivate this as forecast calibration. The method may be tested as an ensemble-relative QDM adaptation, but no universal climate-trend-preservation claim follows.
interpretation.skill: Overall and year-specific metrics are copied from saved tables, with CRPS difference versus RAW on the same product/variable/year. They are descriptive of the existing matched verification, not a new model-quality ranking or causal attribution of skill to crossings. Sorting/relabeling alone cannot change univariate CRPS, means, tercile probabilities or quantile intervals.
minimal_options: Keep formula and clearly label original-rank algebra; disclose observed crossings, dry substitutions and endpoint limitations. This changes no saved forecasts.

Monotone rearrangement: assign sorted corrected values to RAW-sorted member labels. Removes label-order inversions without changing the issued marginal distribution or existing univariate scores. It breaks original-label delta identities and may alter cross-variable/spatial/temporal member dependence; it does not restore the desired distribution-level delta equality.

Change mapping choice to monotone QM, or explicitly fit a constrained monotone quantile-change curve. QM clips tails and is not delta preserving; constrained projection changes corrected values and requires new held-out scoring. Neither is silently applied in this audit.

If climate-change preservation is the aim, define and justify a pooled future/forecast distribution and stationary quantile-bias assumptions before applying QDM; larger pooling changes the estimand and alone does not guarantee no crossings.
interpretation.leakage_scope: The audit pairs only accepted STATUS=OK source-year rows; it neither uses target observations in the oracle nor infers training leakage from current forecast ranks. Full calendar/observation-availability auditing is separate.

primary_source.citation: Cannon, Sobie and Murdock (2015), Bias Correction of GCM Precipitation by Quantile Mapping: How Well Do Methods Preserve Changes in Quantiles and Extremes? Journal of Climate 28, 6938-6959.
primary_source.scope_read: Relevant retrieved sections 1-5a; response later truncated, not a claim to have audited the entire paper.
primary_source.section_3: Projected-series time-dependent CDF is estimated over a time window around t; historical and projected quantiles supply the relative change. This is not automatically equivalent to one conditional issuance ensemble.
primary_source.section_5a: Daily precipitation examples use 30-year sliding windows for projected means/empirical quantiles and pooled sliding seasonal windows. Zeros are replaced by uniform random sub-trace values below 0.05 mm/day before correction and thresholded afterward to handle wet-day frequency.
primary_source.boundary: The audited deterministic tied-midpoint mapping and Qh<0.1 mm replacement on weekly/monthly accumulated rainfall is a different occurrence policy; the daily-paper threshold must not be transplanted without justification. Crossing/rearrangement conclusions here follow executed counterexamples and permutation invariance, not a claim that the paper studied these cases.
